name: Rae Meyer
life: “In my first pension week I practiced unlocking my door just for the sake of coming home.” On Tuesday, near the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, Rae can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I want one key back permanently. Opening my own door is the part of Saturday I look forward to.
appearance: Rae has iron-gray waves, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Rae holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Rae takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Rae can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To get one key back and meet the lunch carrier at the door.
family: Sam Sloan is Rae’s cousin’s child. Rae saves a place. Sam chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *One unposted detour*, Sam says, “I made the map but left out the bakery because it wasn't a registered depot.”
connections: Elizabeth Yoon. They agree which doors will open for a volunteer and which owners will open themselves.
